text:
maya: quick sync — cutover handoff for the canary is scheduled tomorrow 09:30 PT. need alignment on rollback orchestration and chaos scenarios.

alex: thanks — main risks i see: sticky sessions + kv cache staleness during a rollback. if we flip routing back mid-session we might serve mismatched kvs.

sam: agree. i think we should prefer session-neutral fallbacks where possible (route to a smaller/compatible model variant), not a full rollback.

taylor: how bad is inconsistent kv? is it correctness or just perf?

alex: correctness for multi-turn chat. kv cache holds last-turn embeddings and key-values; switching model families can change kv shape/scale.

maya: proposals: 1) sticky affinity with a short grace window (60s) during cutover, 2) proactive kv-warmup for canary nodes, 3) fast fallback to a compatibility shim model. tradeoffs?

jin: affinity + warmup sounds ok, but affinity reduces our ability to shift load quickly if canary blows up. 60s might be long. what about 15s?

priya: ops concern: if we set affinity too short we get split sessions; too long we delay failover. maybe make it configurable per-release and enforce via rollout controller.

sam: controller should understand two classes: safety (latency/error) and quality (regression measured by eval hooks). fallback triggers differ.

maya: yes — safety triggers: p95 latency > 2x baseline or 5xx rate > 1%. quality triggers: eval-set regression > threshold. safety -> immediate routing fallback. quality -> gradual rollback or traffic quarantine.

ops-bot: deploy-check: canary started 09:30 PT; healthchecks green; metric baseline p95=120ms.

alex: need deterministic fallback for cross-region failover. prefer routing by policy: region -> model-variant -> capacity-tier. if primary unavailable, pick variant with matching signature.

jin: discussion on signature matching: we should encode model compatibility labels in catalog metadata (e.g., "kv_shape:v1", "tok_encoding:bytepair"). router can match on labels.

priya: good. also add a quick circuit-breaker state for each route with cooldown backoff: 30s -> 2m -> 8m. that avoids flip-flop during noisy windows.

sam: important: all changes must be idempotent. rollout controller should keep an explicit versioned plan so resumes after controller restart don't double-apply. store plan in etcd with version tag.

maya: example rollout config i sketched:

```
rollout: canary-2026-03
steps:
  - weight: 1%
    duration: 10m
    probes: [latency, error, eval_small]
  - weight: 10%
    duration: 20m
    probes: [latency, error, eval_medium]
  - weight: 50%
    duration: 30m
    probes: [latency, error, eval_full]
fallback:
  safety_policy: immediate_route_to(variant:fast-safe)
  quality_policy: quarantine_route(10m) -> rollback_if(no_improve)
```

maya: the controller must publish events so oncall and release lead can abort manually.

alex: in addition, we should do a staged cutover: drain existing sessions on canary nodes with a soft-drain phase where new sessions go to baseline but existing continue for X seconds. prevents mid-turn model swap.

jin: how do we detect mid-turn? client sends session-token; router checks active-session table. drain window should wait for active sessions to finish or timeout.

priya: timeout needs to be safe for SLAs. we can't wait indefinitely. suggest 45s drain + force-cut to baseline if still active. log those forcibly cut sessions for postmortem.

sam: for revert path, instead of immediate cluster-wide rollback, we can 'escrow' pilot traffic and run a canary patch that only affects new sessions, then escalate if still bad. reduces blast radius.

maya: boolean matrix of triggers we need in runbook:
- safety (latency/5xx) -> immediate fallback variant
- consistency (kv mismatch) -> force affinity + warmup + quarantine
- quality (eval regression) -> hold + rollback after manual review
- infra (resource pressure) -> throttle + route to cheaper variant

alex: telemetry: we must correlate session ids across routing, model variant, and eval artifacts. suggest a trace header x-rd-session that is immutable for session life.

jin: +1. also emit 'handoff' events at router: when a session is moved, emit event with old_variant/new_variant/reason. useful for tracing post-failures.

priya: operational addition: pre-cutover chaos test — simulate 20% node loss and random circuit flips for 5 mins, ensure automated fallback keeps error below 1%. do this in staging tomorrow morning.

ops-bot: chaos-run scheduled: staging 07:00 PT — will post results.

sam: one subtlety: if fallback is to a quantized variant, quality signals might not show obvious regressions immediately but user-facing hallucination could increase later. so add semantic checks in our eval hooks (e.g., classification accuracy, hallucination heuristics).

maya: good point. include semantic eval at step 2 and step 3.

alex: edge-case: some customers use pinned model versions in private deployments; our router must respect customer pinning — fallback only within allowed set or via customer opt-in.

maya: yep, per-tenant policy is required. controller should fail-fast if a rollout would violate a tenant policy.

jin: followup action items:
- alex: add compatibility labels to model catalog (kv_shape, tok_encoding) — due EOD.
- sam: extend rollout controller to publish handoff events + idempotent plan storage — due +2d.
- priya: add circuit-breaker cooldown policy & force-cut logging — due tomorrow morning.
- taylor: run the staging chaos test and share report — scheduled 07:00 PT.

maya: sounds good. if no objections i’ll update the RFC with these changes and add a new rollforward/rollback matrix.

alex: nits: set default affinity to 15s not 60s.

jin: +1 15s.

priya: :thumbsup: 

maya: updated plan: affinity 15s, drain 45s, cooldown backoff 30s/2m/8m. will post RFC diff soon.

ops-bot: note: canary deploy tomorrow 09:30 PT (as maya said). notifications will be sent to #oncall.

sam: thanks everyone. keeping this thread for followups.
